findings.title: Joint Foreign Ministers Statement on Gaza
findings.publisher: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (joint statement: Australia, Canada, Italy and United Kingdom foreign ministers)
findings.affected_population_system: Displaced Gaza residents without adequate winter shelter; humanitarian shelter and aid access
findings.exact_supporting_passage: Yet 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border and prevented from entering Gaza.

discovery_context.discovered_via: WAFA Arabic latest item, followed by direct verification of official GOV.UK statement via UK government news index
discovery_context.material_delta: New coordinated public diplomatic demand by four foreign ministers to end delays, open crossings and allow stranded tents and dual-use humanitarian recovery supplies into Gaza
discovery_context.already_known_context: The winter shelter shortage and broad 150,000-tent quantity were previously reported by OCHA; those are not claimed as new operational measurements
discovery_context.scope_guard: Diplomatic appeal only; no confirmed new shipments, opening of crossings, actual entry of tents, or ceasefire implementation change

coverage_notes.purpose: Supplementary recall only; production collector and publisher remain authoritative.

excluded_candidates: Rafah al-Mawasi drone strike, Khan Younis shooting and Egyptian Red Crescent 2,759-tonne dispatch recorded in 09:53 PST watch.
Previously recorded UNICEF child cumulative casualties, Gaza hospital mortality statistics, UNRWA contracts, recovered remains and Sheikh Radwan casualty.
Previously reported Gaza winter shelter shortage and 150,000-tent volume are background, not a fresh shipment or crossing change.
No separately confirmed new medical evacuation, health-facility capacity shift, border-entry event, ceasefire agreement or hostage development identified during observation interval.
caveats: The official joint statement is dated November 15 but has no published clock time; WAFA's 11:52 PST reporting falls in the preceding watch's cutoff minute, so this is a boundary late recall rather than proven publication after the exact prior end timestamp.
Statements from four foreign ministers are verified as a new coordinated request, not as proof that aid was admitted or crossings reopened.
WHO EMRO returned 502 and Anadolu direct listing timed out, but alternate source coverage remained useful; degraded rather than failed.
Search indexing and reporting lag mean a bounded watch does not rule out uncaptured incidents.
